metadata.content:
That output tells us exactly where we are.
The architecture defines the capability:
TypeScriptdeploymentDiagnostics: boolean;
and the role system exposes it:
TypeScriptdeploymentDiagnostics: true
but there is currently no implementation in the builder UI.
Your grep confirms:


No Diagnostics workspace


No Runtime Health dashboard


No Metrics panel


No Runtime Monitor component


No consumer of /api/runtime/metrics


The runtime side is already partially complete:
✅ /api/runtime/metrics exists
✅ Returns:
JSON{
  "process": {...},
  "totals": {...},
  "runtimes": [...]
}
✅ Registry integration exists
✅ Event bus counters exist
✅ Workspace watcher counters exist
What is missing is the Builder layer.
According to the architecture, the next development task is:
Ticket: Deployment Diagnostics Dashboard
Builder consumes:
httpGET /api/runtime/metrics
and displays:
Runtime Supervisor
Runtime Service
PID
Uptime
RSS Memory
Heap Usage
Runtime Registry
Project
Status
Port
PID
Alive
Uptime
Runtime Totals
Running
Starting
Exited
Error
Watchers
Event Clients
Runtime Actions
Open Logs
Restart Runtime
Stop Runtime
This matches the architecture and leverages code that already exists.
Current status:
LayerStatusRuntime Metrics Endpoint✅ CompleteRuntime Registry Data✅ CompleteRuntime Health Data✅ CompleteBuilder Diagnostics UI❌ MissingDiagnostics Workspace❌ MissingMetrics Polling Hook❌ Missing
So the next architecture-compliant milestone is building the Deployment Diagnostics workspace, not modifying runtime internals.
Before writing code, verify the architecture references it:
Bashgrep -R "deploymentDiagnostics" docs/ architecture/ KORELUMINA_MASTER_ARCHITECTURE.md
and
Bashgrep -R "Runtime Health" docs/ architecture/ KORELUMINA_MASTER_ARCHITECTURE.md
That will identify the exact section to implement against rather than inventing new behavior.
